Micro1 Hackathon - Engineering Scorecard ​

This scorecard translates the official 100-point rubric into actionable engineering and project management tasks.

1. Problem & User Value (15 Points) ​

What the judge is looking for: A clearly defined user with a meaningful bottleneck that actually matters. Evidence needed:

  • A clear description of the user.
  • Explanation of the bottleneck.
  • Why solving it is valuable in practice. Engineering Decisions to Improve Score:
  • Focus on a specific, narrow problem rather than a generic "assistant".
  • Ensure the problem is grounded in a real-world workflow. Mistakes that reduce score:
  • Vague user persona.
  • Solving a non-existent or trivial bottleneck.

2. Agent Solution & Engineering (30 Points) ​

What the judge is looking for: Purposeful use of agents and technically sound implementation. Evidence needed:

  • Code that uses context, tools, memory, verification, skills, or orchestration only when necessary.
  • Explanations of why each design choice was made and how it solved the problem. Engineering Decisions to Improve Score:
  • Justify every agent component.
  • Keep the architecture as simple as possible to achieve the goal reliably. Mistakes that reduce score:
  • Over-engineering (e.g., adding 5 agents when 1 would do).
  • Adding components without a clear, measurable benefit.

3. End to End Quality (20 Points) ​

What the judge is looking for: A realistic, self-contained execution that produces a polished, usable final result. Evidence needed:

  • The final output generated by the agent.
  • A workflow that completes from start to finish without awkward manual interventions (unless explicitly designed as a human checkpoint). Engineering Decisions to Improve Score:
  • Format the output nicely (e.g., structured reports, clean code, proper summaries).
  • Ensure the result does not look like a generic "ChatGPT" draft. Mistakes that reduce score:
  • Output that requires heavy manual editing to be usable.
  • "Obvious AI-generated draft" tone.

4. Measured Improvement (15 Points) ​

What the judge is looking for: Proof that your solution is better than a reasonable baseline. Evidence needed:

  • A simple baseline implementation.
  • The same evaluation cases run on both baseline and agent.
  • A changelog connecting iterations to evidence. Engineering Decisions to Improve Score:
  • Build a solid, fair baseline (don't "sandbag" it).
  • Automate the evaluation of the 10+ cases to prove consistency.
  • Document every iteration, including failures, in the changelog. Mistakes that reduce score:
  • Unfair baseline comparison.
  • Missing changelog entries.
  • Claims of improvement without evidence.

5. Reproducibility (15 Points) ​

What the judge is looking for: The ability to run your project and get the same results from a clean environment. Evidence needed:

  • A comprehensive Reproduction Guide (setup, commands, data, expected output, versions, runtime, cost).
  • Access to the required data (public/synthetic/anonymous). Engineering Decisions to Improve Score:
  • Provide a requirements.txt or package.json.
  • Script the setup process if possible.
  • Avoid hardcoded local paths or relying on private credentials. Mistakes that reduce score:
  • Missing setup instructions.
  • Code that only runs on the creator's machine.
  • Requiring private data the judges cannot access.

6. Hot Take / Insights (5 Points) ​

What the judge is looking for: A practical lesson learned from a failure mode. Evidence needed:

  • An entry in the deliverables documenting a failure mode and the resulting insight. Engineering Decisions to Improve Score:
  • Actively look for edge cases where the agent fails.
  • Document a removed experiment that failed and explain why it failed in the context of building reliable agents. Mistakes that reduce score:
  • Ignoring failures.
  • Providing a generic observation instead of a practical lesson.
